stages.title: Preparation
stages.summary: The header comment (lines 1-30) sets the scene: a virtual IP (VIP) answered by a load balancer is not the balancer device, and the hardware rules refuse the balancer device on purpose. Such hosts belong to the Load Balancer Service CI that models the VIP, and this rule finds it. It runs on the IP field so that VIPs without a DNS name are covered too. The header lists the sample payload, the input (sourceValue is the IP field, and the rule also reads OS and DNS from the payload), what the rule returns (the sys_id of the one Load Balancer Service found by fqdn, then by name, then by address; null when the host shows no VIP evidence, when no service matches, or when two services carry the value) and its place in the chain (after the hardware rules declined, before the IP address rules). A further comment (lines 40-41) explains the ignore list: classes that must never be matched (placeholder and technical CIs), taken from the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass, which the framework may also pass in as _ignoreClass. The code lines here take the inputs and prepare five working values: ip, dns, label, os and ignore.

lines.explanation: A "function" is a named block of instructions that takes inputs and hands back one answer. This line opens a function named process with three inputs: rule (the lookup rule record), sourceValue (the value of the rule's Source field, here the IP) and sourcePayload (the whole Qualys host record). The bracket before the word function means the function is written and run in one go; the last line of the script supplies the inputs.

stages.title: The real servers, exactly one (the search and the answer)
stages.summary: The second part of the last stage (comments at lines 210-220): for each member, the address is searched on Hardware records, on Network Adapters that belong to a CI, and on IP Address records whose adapter belongs to a CI; then the member's relationships to hardware are followed. Every hit goes through keep(). Finally the distinct servers are counted and the single one is returned. Sample: the address "10.10.20.31" finds only "usvacrispweb01" on the Hardware table; adapters, IP Address records and relationships give nothing; one server, so <usvacrispweb01> is the answer. The closing line runs the whole function.
